cartesian-mill-pocket.reason: The V1 and V2 cases cover the same milling toolpath and command acceptance; neither simulator verifies spindle output.

pause-resume.reason: The V2 simulation checks M600/M601 messages, commands sent while suspended, and the saved-position restore; real host cooperation is not tested.

laser-raster.reason: The V1 and V2 cases exercise the same raster motion and commands; neither step trace validates laser PWM or emitted power.

emergency-stop.reason: The V1 case uses M112, for which the inspected V2 firmware has no handler; the V2 kill-input case exercises a different halt path.
emergency-stop.review: At V2 firmware revision e9eef522aa4bae253027f2ac36e247e20b4e362c, no M112 handler was found in Firmware/src. Dispatcher.cpp returns false for unhandled commands and Consoles.cpp reports them as ignored. The V2 host simulator instead aborts on an unhandled M112; neither observation is a physical-board test.

arcs-radius.reason: V2 firmware rejects radius-mode G2 and G3, so the V1 radius-arc motion scenario does not apply.
arcs-radius.review: At firmware revision e9eef522aa4bae253027f2ac36e247e20b4e362c, Firmware/src/robot/Robot.cpp checks for an R argument on either arc mode and returns a radius-mode-not-supported error instead of calling process_move. The separately reviewed case checks rejection and halt, not radius-arc motion.
